text:
Alex P: FYI multiple customers hitting 502/504s on hosted /v1/embeddings since ~10:21 UTC, started as a small spike and then sustained. Seen on eu1 and us-west. sample req id: req-0a7f, trace: trc-9b2. Can someone triage? :eyes:

Maria G: Noted. Are these large-batch embed requests or single small ones? Any repro curl?

Alex P: Mix — mostly batches of 100+ inputs. Repro with this curl produced a 502 for me:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large","inputs":["x"] * 120}'
```

Jordan L: I ran a quick smoke against eu1 and got 502s with envoy upstream resets. curl output:
```
HTTP/2 502
server: envoy
content-type: text/plain

upstream reset before response completed
```
Trace in edge: trace=trc-9b2 req=req-0a7f upstream_id=shadow-proxy-03

SRE Bot: auto-alert: edge.gateway.errors spike > baseline (10m) — created incident IM-1716500000. Logs linked: https://logs.internal/trace/trc-9b2

Maria G: Poking Envoy logs. Seeing a burst of 504s then 502s with upstream connect failures to shadow-proxy nodes. Sample log:
```
[2026-03-18T10:21:04Z] envoy upstream reset: code=UPSTREAM_CONNECTION_FAILURE cluster=shadow-proxy cluster_manager: connection failure to 10.4.9.21:8080
[2026-03-18T10:21:06Z] request timeout waiting for upstream response, route: /v1/embeddings
```

Sophie K: Related: we pushed an auth cache TTL tweak in eu1 ~09:58 that tightened cache keys and increased cache misses. Could cause auth circuit or add extra upstreams. Any auth errors in the logs?

Jordan L: Good call — auth backend latency jumped at 10:20 from 20ms -> 180ms and auth cache miss rate up 8x. Edge shows many auth fetches to shadow-proxy rather than cache hit. Example: auth service logs:
```
[2026-03-18T10:20:59Z] auth.lookup miss tenant=acme request=req-0a7f latency=182ms
[2026-03-18T10:21:01Z] auth.lookup miss tenant=beta latency=195ms
```

Alex P: So hypothesis: auth cache TTL tweak => cache miss storm for batch requests => shadow-proxy auth fetches amplify upstream load => upstream connections hit resource limits and start resetting -> 502/504 at edge.

Oncall: For mitigation can we temporarily revert TTL tweak or enable a short local cache on the edge for auth tokens? Also suggest throttling batch size from SDK side until we stabilize.

Maria G: Rolling back auth cache change in eu1 now (rollback started). Also increasing Envoy upstream retry and connection pool to shadow-proxy cluster as short-term.

SRE Bot: change rollback triggered by @Maria G at 2026-03-18T10:23:14Z. Monitoring for recovery.

Jordan L: After rollback new requests show normal auth cache hit rate and error rate trending down. curl now returns 200 for same batch sample.

Alex P: Noted — telling affected customers we mitigated, asking them to validate. Will keep thread open for 1h to confirm stability. :thumbsup:

Sophie K: Follow-ups: add a canary for auth cache changes, add load simulation when changing TTL, and add a protective local edge cache for short TTLs. Filing follow-up ticket ENG-Auth-772.
